title:
ESG Initiatives and Corporate Performance:
Evidence from Environmental and Diversity Practices in S&P 500 Firms
content: We examine the relationship between ESG initiatives and corporate performance using 360 S&P 500 firms from 2010 to 2018. Employing MSCI ESG ratings and controlling for industry and time effects, we find that environmental initiatives positively correlate with profitability (ROA), while gender diversity associates with growth prospects (Tobin's Q). Results are robust to alternative specifications, propensity score matching, and instrumental variable approaches. A one-standard-deviation increase in environmental performance corresponds to a 0.9 percentage point increase in ROA (approximately $127 million annually for the median firm). Our findings are consistent with stakeholder theory and the resource-based view, though we cannot definitively establish causality. The study contributes standardized evidence on specific ESG dimensions using rigorous empirical methods.
